reason: Exhaustive runtime probe (tool event t6, run_claim_probe on CUDA) tested every one of the 63,488 finite FP16 input encodings — the complete public domain per problem.txt, including signed zeros, subnormals, and largest positive/negative finite values — comparing kernel.run() output bit patterns against a 60-digit mpmath sigmoid reference with manual round-to-nearest-even FP16 selection. Mismatch count: 0. This directly tests the contract's exact FP16 bit-pattern requirement over the whole domain and confirms the kernel's FP64 exp/div plus single cvt.rn.f16.f64 rounding strategy is correctly rounded everywhere. Claim c1 (that at least one legal input fails bit-exact matching) is rebutted. Source inspection confirms output is a fresh empty_like tensor of matching shape/dtype/device and the input is untouched. No in-scope contract violation was found.
